summary.headline: AAVAS Q1FY27: net profit up 23% YoY to Rs 1.71 bn, NII up 18%, but management sees spread falling below 5% over the year.
summary.overview: Disbursements rose 41% YoY to Rs 16.1 bn on a low base, and AUM grew 15.4% YoY to Rs 239.3 bn as of June end. NIM rose 22 bps YoY to 7.70% and cost-to-income improved 254 bps to 43.7%. Asset quality metrics improved YoY, with 1+DPD at 3.76% and gross Stage 3 at 1.11%. Management flagged spread pressure from competition and a 10 bps PLR cut in June, taking the cumulative cut to 25 bps since March 2026, and an intent to regain home loan share.

segments.name: Home loans (HL)
segments.commentary: HL disbursement volumes grew 17% YoY in Q1 per management, and the company is refocusing on HL to rebalance the HL/NHL book toward roughly 65:35. HL carries 150-200 bps lower yield than NHL.

segments.name: Non-housing loans (NHL: LAP, MSME)
segments.commentary: Management described NHL as LAP and MSME products. The company said it has no builder loan product.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: 22-23% top-line growth and 17-18% AUM growth; medium-term AUM growth of about 20%.
Management expects spread to fall to just below 5% over the rest of the year, while still expecting ROA and ROE to hold at planned levels.
Target to lift productivity per field resource from Rs 8-10 lakh to Rs 20-22 lakh, to be achieved in about two years.
June disbursements exceeded Rs 600 crore; management aims to keep disbursements on a high run-rate through the next nine months.
Management reiterated credit-quality guidance and said it is confident of holding it.
capex_capacity: Branch network expanded to 440 branches across 15 states during Q1; further branch expansion planned, with focus on faster branch break-even.
Borrowing liquidity: cash, cash equivalents and unavailed CC limits of Rs 18.8 bn; documented unavailed sanctions of Rs 4.85 bn as of June 30, 2026.
demand_pricing: Healthy competition across geographies with spread pressure; management said it is consciously pursuing HL share regain, which will cost some NIM.
Monthly AUM additions rose nearly 50% YoY; management said the company now reaches in three months what took about five months previously.
PLR cut 10 bps effective June 2026 (cumulative 25 bps since March 2026), with the company saying disbursement yield and portfolio yield are now close to each other.
Repayment rates rose to above 19% in the last two quarters versus a historical 16-17%; the uptick was in April and early May, especially in small-ticket loans above 14% interest, and eased in June.

Borrowings: 42% linked to external benchmarks (Repo, T-Bill, MIBOR) and 34% to sub-3-month MCLR, so about 76% reprices quickly; average borrowing tenor is longer than asset tenor, giving positive ALM.

qa_highlights.question: How intense is competition by product and geography, and can operating leverage offset spread compression?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees healthy competition and spread pressure, and expects spread to go below 5% for the full year. It says cost-to-income and revenue-per-resource levers should keep ROE and ROA near plan, even with some compression.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the repayment rate rising, and what is the June disbursement run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Repayments rose in April and early May in small-ticket segments above 14%, then came back to trend in June. June disbursements were above Rs 600 crore, and the company is targeting 22-23% disbursement growth and 17-18% AUM growth over the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the disbursement per branch that underpins the medium-term 20% AUM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected that current-year guidance is 17-18% AUM growth, with 20% as the medium-term target. Productivity is to rise from Rs 8-10 lakh to Rs 20-22 lakh per field resource, which management said it would shorten to two years.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company regain home loan market share, given a low two-year CAGR in HL files?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants to rebalance HL and NHL toward about 65:35, with branch-level targeted acquisition for the next 9-12 months. HL volumes were up 17% YoY in Q1. It accepts a small NIM compression from the HL push.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gap between disbursement yield and portfolio yield after the June PLR cut, and what is the spread outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the two yields are now nearly equal and the reported yield and spread already reflect the June cut. It expects spread to fall a little below 5% for the rest of the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the recent RBI asset classification circular on repossessed assets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the circular is under evaluation and any required change will be made.

risks_watch: Spread compression below 5% from competition and PLR cuts, with HL push adding further NIM pressure.
Stress in tours and travel and restaurant segments, linked to the Middle East conflict and fuel prices; the company tightened policies from February. Rainfall shortfall is also a watch item.
Repayment and part-prepayment trends in small-ticket, higher-yield loans; management says June normalised.
Pending evaluation of the RBI asset-classification circular on repossessed assets.
Interim CFO in place, and the CEO appointment is subject to RBI approval.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, execution and asset quality, while openly acknowledging spread pressure and the cost of the home loan push. Management gave a clear spread view (below 5%) and said ROA and ROE should hold. Some answers were hedged, such as the RBI circular impact, which is still under evaluation.
key_quotes: As I look for the complete year, I do believe that spread compression from the existing point will take spread to go sub-5%.
Reasonably confident to make sure that the ROE and ROA that we have planned for the year remains where it is, even if slight compression does take place on the competitive environment.
I am heavily focused on regaining our market share in the HL segment, which is the primary aim of the HFC.

adds.what: Branch network expanded to 440 branches across 15 states during Q1; further branch expansion planned

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 top-line growth of 22-23% and AUM growth of 17-18%, with medium-term AUM growth of about 20%, backed by 440 branches (added in Q1), June disbursements above Rs 600 crore, and monthly AUM additions up ~50% YoY, though no concrete capacity or order numbers were given and management expects spread to fall below 5%.
